articles.title: FPIs pull out Rs 52,100 cr from equities in Oct so far amid global headwinds
articles.content: Foreign portfolio investors have withdrawn Rs 52,100 crore from Indian equities as of October this year. This follows a net withdrawal of Rs 35,861 crore in September, indicating ongoing financial retreat. Elevated crude oil prices, higher US bond yields, and a stronger dollar have affected investor sentiment. Despite temporary buying by foreign investors on October 16, selling in certain sectors continues.

articles.title: YES Bank Q2 profit rises 65%; AT1 hit may risk 5,217 cr loss

The bank's privatization, through the sale to Fairfax, aims to enhance performance and profitability.

articles.title: AI race may depend more on access to power, infrastructure than chip supply: Morgan Stanley

articles.title: Crypto’s leverage machine finds new life beyond Bitcoin bets
articles.content: Despite a decline in crypto trading activities, there is a rising interest in traditional assets among investors. Open interest in real-world asset contracts has increased to $9 billion, claiming 14% of total volume. The transition marks a significant change in the derivatives markets as crypto inroads are being utilized for traditional trading. This shift indicates a maturation of the digital asset space, making it more accessible to mainstream investors.
